entries.claim: The inspected NewAPI source declares existing routes for login, refresh, self, user models, top-up, pricing, and session management.
The inspected NewAPI pricing model exposes model ID, input/output/cache ratios, billing mode/expression, enabled groups, endpoint types, and a pricing version.
The inspected NewAPI pricing UI derives token input price from model_ratio multiplied by two and by a selected or available group ratio, then applies output and cache multipliers.

The inspected NewAPI pricing response structure has pricing values and a pricing version but no explicit official-source URL, official verification timestamp, or field declaring that the base value is a vendor official price.

The inspected NewAPI models.dev ratio importer selects the cheapest non-zero provider price for duplicate model names, so imported base ratios are not mechanically guaranteed to be the model vendor's own official price.

The inspected CC Switch implementation discovers supported CLIs through the PATH-default command plus audited fallback directories, executes bounded --version probes, distinguishes not-found from installed-but-broken, and has separate Windows command-script and App Execution Alias handling.

Read-only requests to the deployed first-party origins on 2026-08-30 returned system name 野菜API and version v1.0.0-rc.27 from both /api/status endpoints, HTTP 404 for /api/desktop/v1/bootstrap, HTTP 401 for unauthenticated /api/user/self, and a public /api/pricing projection containing 37 models plus pricing_version a42d372ccf0b5dd13ecf71203521f9d2. This verifies current public behavior only and does not establish a deployed desktop authorization or stable desktop pricing projection.

The locally installed official @deepseek-ai/dsh package is version 0.1.0-rc.6, points to github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness, and documents dsh web as the web-profile alias, but its public CLI documentation does not establish a stable user-owned Base URL field or a safe automatic-write adapter contract.

The first governed RU-003 verification run executed five scenarios successfully but the catalog scenario failed because invoking Vitest inside the mandatory read-only source sandbox attempted to create vitest.config.ts.timestamp-*.mjs in the project root. After replacing that nested runner with direct Node TypeScript module execution, local execution passed all six scenarios; redispatch was then blocked because the dispatcher revalidated the completed RU-002 dependency against RU-003's intentionally superseding current UI outputs.

At commit 72644de the desktop shell has truthful account and billing unavailable states, a five-tool read-only local scan, and a five-tool two-line configuration preview, but it has no home guidance destination, no line-connectivity query, no settings and security destination, bundle output is disabled, updater artifacts are disabled, and the Tauri runtime exposes only scan_tools_read_only.

Current code fixes Claude internal model to Sonnet, overwrites request models in both bridges, persists one model per tool, drops some SSE errors, imposes 60-second read idle, and waits unbounded for activation lock on quit. Windows credential blob limit is 2560 bytes.

Active AppLibraryView missing-app CTA only navigates to configuration; active native commands contain discovery/configuration but no installer. RU-045 receipts show private staging, not public downloads; official raw packages and current-user app discovery can support a separate client workflow without changing existing vendor apps or NewAPI.

RU-043 historical verification failed only its typecheck/build command due to an unused React import in preview.tsx; native and renderer commands passed but the package never completed. Current preview already uses only useState and a fresh node typescript/bin/tsc --noEmit exits 0. RU-046 dispatch correctly refused this incomplete dependency. Re-run all prior acceptance commands on the current read-only tree under a reviewed successor instead of treating partial evidence as complete.

entries.claim: The current official NewAPI GitHub HEAD 918427d8ab41f6adaa4113d0496f1f8621855b70 exposes browser login, refresh-cookie, current-user, pricing, usage-log, and top-up routes, but no /api/desktop/v1 device-authorization boundary. Its documented browser session keeps a 15-minute access token in browser memory and a rotating HttpOnly SameSite=Strict refresh cookie, so it is not a safe drop-in desktop-device credential contract.

The current official Codex configuration reference documents ~/.codex/config.toml, model_providers.<id>.base_url, responses-only wire_api, and model_providers.<id>.auth.command as a command that prints a bearer token to stdout; auth.command must not be combined with env_key, experimental_bearer_token, or requires_openai_auth.

The current official Claude Code documentation identifies ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL as the custom endpoint setting and apiKeyHelper as a dynamic script-based credential source, supporting a preview of owned settings without placing a literal API key in settings.

The current official OpenCode provider documentation defines custom providers under provider.<id>, uses @ai-sdk/openai-compatible for OpenAI-compatible chat-completions endpoints, accepts options.baseURL, and identifies model entries by their exact model IDs.

The current official Pi models documentation identifies ~/.pi/agent/models.json, provider baseUrl and api fields, exact model IDs, OpenAI-compatible API modes, and an apiKey value beginning with ! as a command evaluated at request time.

Current official Tauri v2 distribution guidance supports platform-specific installers and states that direct macOS distribution requires code signing and notarization while Windows distribution provides installer and code-signing paths.
Current Apple guidance requires appropriate Developer ID signing, hardened runtime, secure timestamping, notarization review, and testing for directly distributed macOS software.

Current Microsoft guidance states that unsigned downloads can show SmartScreen warnings, may be blocked by enterprise policy or Smart App Control, and do not carry publisher reputation between versions.

Current Tauri v2 updater guidance requires signed update artifacts, keeps the verification public key in the client, and requires the signing private key only in the protected build environment; update signature verification cannot be disabled.

Claude supports full-ID inferenceModels with display-only labels; Codex loads a custom catalog at startup; OpenAI SDK uses a 600-second inference timeout default. These support bounded implementation choices, not live relay compatibility.

OpenAI publishes official Mac Apple Silicon DMG and Windows x64/ARM64 MSIX; Claude publishes Mac universal DMG and Windows MSIX. Add-AppxPackage installs signed packages per user and handles dependencies without AllowUnsigned. Claude Cowork may require separate administrator-managed services/reboot. Native installation and account/model connectivity are distinct. Original-app signatures and OS protections must be retained.

Windows App Installer uses the local signed MSIX and asks for user confirmation; opening the dialog is not successful signature verification or installation. It can offer Reinstall, so Yecai must never claim to prevent a user-authorized OS replacement. The ms-appinstaller web protocol is disabled by default; use the downloaded local package. Zig's real Windows resource compiler was used to provide missing developer RC compilation without skipping resources.

RU-002 should preserve the verified RU-001 discovery experience and add a client-only account and billing shell whose sole runtime account projection is backend_upgrade_required. It must show no fabricated account, balance, usage, price, authorization, or wallet result and must make no production account request until a later frozen unit verifies the least-privilege desktop server contract.

RU-003 should add a deterministic beginner configuration-preview planner for the fixed five-tool catalog and the two product-approved line roots. It may show only evidenced target fields and derived protocol endpoints, must leave the model ID unavailable until a server catalog exists, and must block all configuration, credential, file-read, file-write, connectivity, and rollback actions until later backend, secure-helper, and exact-version evidence is frozen.

A verification-only successor release unit should preserve RU-003 product behavior and source exactly, use the corrected direct-module acceptance scenario under the mandatory read-only sandbox, retain the original failed run as historical evidence, and avoid replaying the dispatcher dependency check that compares intentionally superseded UI outputs to RU-002.

RU-005 should supersede RU-004 and finish the bounded client-side V1 candidate by adding a guided home, user-triggered secret-free DNS and TCP-443 diagnostics for only the two approved line hosts, a settings and security truth surface, complete multilingual page states, candidate bundle configuration, and platform and backend handoff checklists while login, models, prices, credentials, configuration writes, retained backups, telemetry upload, signed updates, and production release remain unavailable.
野菜API is an official desktop client whose first priority includes account access, balance, recharge, and usage visibility.
The current phase changes only the desktop client; NewAPI, servers, Nginx, and production configuration remain unchanged.
Desktop authorization is first-party authorization by the 野菜API website, not direct third-party provider login inside the client.
V1 serves novice users who already installed their AI tools but do not know how to configure them; tool installation is deferred.
V1 supports Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Pi, and DSH (DeepSeek Harness).
The mainland-optimized and Cloudflare global-acceleration lines share the same account, API key, model availability, and pricing semantics; only the network path differs.

The default model list shows models available to the current account and compatible with the selected tool; all models may be viewed with unavailable entries disabled and explained, and a removed model is never silently substituted.
The desktop client compares the official-price baseline already configured in NewAPI with the current user's NewAPI price; it must not maintain a second independent numeric official-price table.

NewAPI model_ratio, model_price, and base billing expressions are always maintained as the corresponding vendor official price; all 野菜API discounts are layered separately through user group ratios or explicit special billing rules.

The desktop account login uses first-party device authorization: the client opens the system browser for website login and explicit device approval, polls for completion, never places passwords, cookies, API keys, or final session credentials in the URL, handles cancellation and expiry explicitly, and supports website-side device revocation.

Desktop device authorization codes are single-use and expire after 10 minutes; access tokens last one hour and refresh automatically; the remembered device session expires after 30 days of inactivity and has a 90-day absolute reauthorization limit; logout, website revocation, and refresh failure are explicit invalidation paths, while sensitive account actions remain on the first-party website.

The desktop account session uses least privilege: it may read the current account profile, balance, usage, available models, and prices and manage only the current device's per-tool relay keys and logout. Password, email, payment data, recharge records, user groups, other devices, other-device key plaintext, and administrative settings remain website-only or inaccessible.

The product owner accepted the exact-version compatibility allowlist for V1: automatic configuration is enabled only for exact tool versions that passed the complete matrix, while unknown, newly released, failed, and otherwise unverified versions remain read-only until a trusted compatibility update adds them.

The product owner authorized development to begin with a governed first release unit limited to the 野菜API desktop shell, product branding, and read-only discovery and compatibility reporting for Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Pi, and DSH; account login, billing, recharge, NewAPI changes, secrets, configuration writes, automatic updates, and telemetry are excluded from this unit.

The product owner authorized the next client development unit for first-party website authorization, account balance and usage, recharge entry, and official-versus-actual price presentation while preserving the existing decision that NewAPI, servers, Nginx, and production configuration are not changed in the current phase.

The product owner authorized implementation to continue after RU-002 and accepted starting the next client-only one-click configuration foundation while preserving the decision not to modify NewAPI, servers, Nginx, DNS, databases, or production configuration in this phase.

The product owner authorized one continuous goal to finish the client-side 野菜API V1 candidate without incremental approval pauses, while preserving the existing prohibition on changing NewAPI, servers, Nginx, DNS, databases, or production and without fabricating backend-dependent success.
User approves the diagnosed model identity, multi-model native switching and Windows exit improvements, and supplies a screenshot showing request retry after 1m3s. No packaging or server changes.

decisions.question: What client-only successor release unit is authorized after RU-001 when the deployed NewAPI still lacks the approved desktop authorization boundary?
decisions.choice: Freeze RU-002 as a successor to RU-001. Preserve the branded five-tool read-only discovery experience and add the production account and billing information architecture, complete page states, fixed display-only 1 USD = 6.75 CNY context, and an updated future NewAPI change specification. The only runtime account projection in this unit is backend_upgrade_required: it performs no account network request, stores no credential, shows no fabricated account or numeric billing value, and exposes no active recharge or authorization action until a later frozen unit verifies a deployed least-privilege /api/desktop/v1 contract.

decisions.question: How should the accepted RU-003 implementation be verified after the original frozen acceptance runner proved incompatible with mandatory read-only isolation and redispatch rechecked superseded dependency outputs?
decisions.choice: Create RU-004 as a verification-only successor to RU-003. Preserve the RU-003 product scope, source, contract, page, and blocked side-effect boundary without modification; execute the same six semantic scenarios using the corrected direct Node TypeScript module loader plus read-only source assertions; retain the original failed run as immutable historical evidence; and declare no work-package dependency because RU-004 changes no implementation and its release-unit dependency and supersession preserve the authority chain.

decisions.question: What bounded implementation unit may finish the client-side V1 candidate after RU-004 without implying that backend-dependent or release-security capabilities are ready?
decisions.choice: Freeze RU-005 as a client-side V1 candidate successor that supersedes RU-004. Preserve the account, billing, five-tool discovery, and configuration-preview truth boundaries; add one beginner home journey, a user-triggered read-only diagnostic that resolves and attempts TCP port 443 only for yeschoy.com and api.yeschoy.com without credentials or API payloads, and a settings and security surface that exposes language, privacy, secret, backup, update, and release state. Prepare but do not publish Windows and macOS candidate bundles, keep updater artifacts and telemetry upload disabled, label Windows unsigned beta limitations and macOS signing and notarization as unmet release gates, and update the future NewAPI handoff without modifying any server or production resource.

decisions.question: How should the approved novice installer follow-up resolve real workflow defects and obsolete tests without weakening installation or connection safety?
decisions.choice: Create RU-051 as a bounded successor to completed RU-050, retaining desktop-app-installation v2 and desktop-tool-activation v8. Fix false macOS presence, selected-app recovery after a different native job terminates, and logged-out Windows confirmation while preserving no-overwrite and exact session/intent consent. Migrate only obsolete App integration expectations to the actual Yecai workbench, retaining provider/hook/component coverage. Require fresh whole-repository Vitest, native tests, Windows/Apple-Silicon compile checks and production build; prior scoped green evidence is not whole-product readiness. Public mirror authorization and clean-machine hardware remain external evidence gaps, not a reason to disable checking an installation. Do not package, publish or change the server in this unit.
decisions.decidedBy: primary engineer under product-owner follow-up approval, with independent read-only workflow audit

terms.definition: 由野菜API网站授权给桌面客户端、只用于账户和客户端管理接口的凭证状态。
依据当前用户、计费分组、模型、缓存、阶梯和价格版本计算的野菜API价格。
面向用户的 API 接入入口类别，例如大陆优化或全球线路；实际端点在高级信息中可见。
请求和本地工具配置中使用的真实模型标识，不得被推荐标签取代或隐藏。
模型厂商公开价格源在指定核对时间、单位和计费条件下声明的价格。
本地配置写入、读取回验和工具所需协议的最小连通性测试均成功后的状态。

requirements.statement: The target client account flow uses first-party browser authorization and then displays account balance, usage, and recharge entry points.
acceptance: The client never asks the user to choose GitHub or LinuxDo as a desktop-specific login provider.
If the website session is absent, the website performs its normal login before authorization.
The device code is short-lived and single-use, and the client exposes waiting, approved, rejected, expired, cancelled, and network-interrupted states.
Passwords, website cookies, API keys, and final desktop session credentials never appear in an authorization URL.
The website names and revokes authorized devices, and the client obeys revocation on its next online request.
A device code expires after 10 minutes, an access token after one hour, an inactive remembered session after 30 days, and every device requires reauthorization no later than 90 days.
The issued device session contains only the approved current-account read and current-device key-management scopes.
A backend device/authorization contract is specified before this target flow is implemented.

requirements.statement: The client displays balance and usage and opens the existing first-party wallet page in the system browser for recharge during V1.
acceptance: Balance and usage identify freshness and retry state.
Recharge does not embed payment credentials or duplicate payment settlement in the client.
Password, email, payment data, recharge-record mutation, and other sensitive account actions remain on the first-party website.
The external wallet destination is restricted to the configured first-party origin.

requirements.statement: Model facts have explicit owners: NewAPI live data owns current-account availability, exact IDs, the numeric official-price baseline, and actual user pricing; a versioned first-party catalog owns compatibility, recommendations, descriptions, and any price provenance metadata not yet returned by NewAPI, but never a duplicate price number.
acceptance: No client-side fuzzy match changes an exact server model ID.
A newly available model without catalog metadata remains identifiable but is not declared compatible without evidence.
The client derives both comparison values from NewAPI's pricing semantics and never embeds an independently maintained numeric official-price table.
The bundled catalog is covered by the signed client artifact and may supplement source and verification metadata until a versioned server contract supersedes it.
NewAPI model_ratio, model_price, and base billing expressions remain vendor official prices; discounts and promotions are represented only by separately identifiable group or special billing rules.
Automatically imported aggregator or channel prices cannot overwrite an official baseline until they are verified against the corresponding vendor source.
Tiered expressions, per-request prices, media units, current-user groups, and special pricing rules are preserved rather than reduced to a universal multiplier formula.

requirements.statement: RU-001 provides a beginner-readable 野菜API desktop shell that performs only local read-only discovery of Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Pi, and DSH and reports exact detected versions and conservative compatibility truth without contacting a server or changing the machine.
acceptance: The primary screen names 野菜API and explains in plain language that it is checking already-installed tools without asking for an API key, Base URL, model name, or configuration-file path.

One explicit scan returns exactly one result for each of Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Pi, and DSH and distinguishes not found, detected but unverified, executable failure or timeout, and ambiguous multiple-installation states.

Every detected version string remains visible; a version not present in a later verified exact-version allowlist is reported as read-only and exposes no configure, repair, remove, install, line, model, credential, login, billing, recharge, updater, or telemetry action.
The scan performs no HTTP or other network request, does not read tool configuration contents, does not access a credential store, and creates, modifies, or deletes no user or tool file.
A failed or timed-out probe affects only that tool card, keeps the other tool results visible, provides a safe rescan action, and never guesses installation or compatibility.
Repeated scans replace stale results by request identity so an older completion cannot overwrite the newest visible scan.

requirements.statement: RU-002 preserves RU-001 and adds a beginner-readable account and billing shell that truthfully reports the missing desktop backend boundary without contacting account services, storing credentials, fabricating values, or enabling recharge.
acceptance: The shell exposes clear Account and Local tools destinations and preserves the complete fixed five-tool read-only scan behavior from RU-001.
The account destination states that secure website authorization requires a future server upgrade and exposes no control that pretends authorization can currently begin or complete.
Balance, today usage, month usage, model ID, official price, actual price, and recharge remain visibly unavailable instead of showing zero, sample, cached, or inferred values.
The fixed 1 USD = 6.75 CNY comparison rate is labelled display-only and not presented as a live exchange rate or a billing input.

The runtime makes no account, pricing, usage, authorization, wallet, or other network request and persists no password, website cookie, access token, refresh token, API key, account profile, or scan history.

The updated future NewAPI specification is pinned to current official GitHub evidence, distinguishes current routes from proposed /api/desktop/v1 routes, and records the deployed 404 readiness result without changing NewAPI or production infrastructure.

requirements.statement: RU-003 preserves RU-002 and adds a beginner-readable local configuration preview for Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Pi, and DSH across the mainland-optimized and global-accelerated lines without reading or changing any tool configuration, accessing a credential, contacting a server, or inventing a model ID.
acceptance: The configuration destination presents exactly Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Pi, and DSH in stable order and lets the user choose exactly one tool for the current preview.
The line step presents exactly mainland optimized at https://yeschoy.com and global accelerated at https://api.yeschoy.com, and the selected line root remains visible in the summary.

Claude Code previews the approved root URL, Codex, OpenCode, and Pi preview the selected root with /v1, and DSH explicitly withholds a protocol endpoint and write target because its exact web-profile adapter is not verified.
The preview names only evidenced user-owned fields, exposes no literal secret or complete user path, and clearly states that it has not read an existing configuration.
Model ID remains visibly unavailable pending the first-party model catalog; the UI displays no sample model, guessed model, price, connectivity result, or supported-version claim.
The apply control remains disabled and the projection reports networkAttempted, configurationRead, configurationWritten, and credentialAccessed as false for every tool and line selection.
RU-001 local discovery and RU-002 account and billing readiness behavior remain available and unchanged, and no NewAPI, server, Nginx, DNS, database, updater, or production resource is modified.

requirements.statement: RU-005 preserves all prior truthful client boundaries and completes a cohesive client-side V1 candidate with beginner guidance, bounded two-line connectivity evidence, settings and security truth, complete multilingual states, candidate bundle preparation, and an actionable future NewAPI handoff without claiming production or backend readiness.
acceptance: The default destination gives a beginner one ordered path through local tool discovery, line choice and preview, account integration truth, and diagnostics, with no API, Base URL, configuration-file, or secret knowledge required.

The account and billing destination still displays no fabricated login, balance, usage, model ID, official price, actual price, or recharge result, and configuration apply remains disabled for every tool and line.

Connectivity runs only after an explicit user action, checks exactly yeschoy.com:443 and api.yeschoy.com:443 through a closed local query, returns only bounded DNS and TCP outcomes with latency and correlation, sends no HTTP or model request, and never accesses or uploads a credential, cookie, prompt, response, configuration, complete local path, or raw network error.

The diagnostic UI distinguishes default, processing, partial success, complete failure, stale result, invalid projection, and recovery, and explicitly says TCP reachability does not prove API, account, model, or billing health.

Settings makes language selection, no-retained-backup policy, secret boundary, inactive telemetry upload, inactive updater, candidate version, and release gates visible without exposing an action that exceeds current authority.

A candidate-only Tauri bundle overlay exists for local Windows and macOS packaging while automatic updater artifacts remain disabled; the release checklist requires native-platform builds, macOS Developer ID signing and notarization for direct public distribution, and an explicit unsigned-Windows beta warning until a real signing path exists.
All four supported languages contain the candidate navigation and page copy, the UI remains usable at 320 CSS pixels, and keyboard focus remains visible.

The future NewAPI handoff names the exact interfaces needed for authorization, bootstrap, account, usage, models, server-projected official-versus-actual prices, tool keys, telemetry, compatibility catalog, and update separation while recording that none is deployed or modified by RU-005.

requirements.statement: Implement explicitly selected model sets with real identity and fixed per-model billing routes, honest request errors and cooperative bounded exit without packaging or server mutation.
acceptance: Up to the documented 200-entry catalog bound, unique full model IDs bind explicit billing groups; default is a member. No silent cross-group fallback or enrollment of unselected models. Legacy records upgrade on explicit activation only.

All seven adapters publish native model menus/catalogs via authenticated loopback routing; legitimate native default changes are not configuration corruption. In-flight requests retain their route. Unsupported optional vendor menus do not block default use.
Credential sets remain inside OS credential storage, handle the Windows per-blob bound transactionally, and never expose full keys through renderer, files, errors or diagnostics.

Claude identity uses real IDs rather than Sonnet display masking; both bridges route requested model exactly and isolate continuation history. Curated HTTP/SSE errors and in-memory last-request observations never turn failed streams into success.

Window close offers background/cancel/exit globally. Confirmed exit rejects new operations, cancels safe work, preserves in-flight account mutations and local rollback, and stops owned runtimes with bounded grace and recoverable progress.

Synthetic transaction/route/stream/exit tests, actual renderer tests/typecheck/build and Windows compilation pass. No installer, signed release, server change or live-account success is inferred from these tests.

requirements.statement: Provide novice install-and-connect with native Mac installation, explicit Windows system installation confirmation, guided other clients, and exact one-use session-bound connection handoff.
acceptance: Missing desktop apps offer installation without architecture/path/command choices; existing applications retain ordinary connect/open/restore. Other clients clearly offer official installation guidance.

Only compiled original HTTPS sources and package identities are accepted. Exact redirect, size/type, owned-file and cache validator checks precede native trust. No arbitrary URL/path/command, account credentials, public mirror publication or forced update.

Mac verifies codesign/Team/bundle/Gatekeeper, stages privately, and publishes exclusively without replacement. Windows checks manifest identity/publisher/architecture, opens the hash-bound local package in system App Installer, explicitly leaves trust pending, and never silently deploys. Tell users to cancel Reinstall/Replace; OS installation choices remain user-owned.

Single request-idempotent native job; safe download cancellation and validator-bound resume, same-package hash reuse and recoverable progress across navigation. Bad metadata, signatures, partial bodies, races, ambiguous targets and lost responses cannot claim completion.

Mac automatic continuation and explicitly confirmed Windows continuation use an exact job-associated native target and one-use full model/group/default/line intent bound to the native session epoch. Renderer selection/navigation revisions invalidate A-to-B-to-A continuations. Fresh native/account/model validation remains mandatory.

Mac mutation drains under existing shutdown admission, including worker errors and cleanup. Windows releases admission after safe system-UI handoff; Yecai cancellation/exit does not cancel Windows installation. A failed connection leaves the installed app in place and uses existing settings recovery.

Use accessible progress and actionable source/network/space/trust/dependency/permission recovery, not engineering jargon. Fixture/cross-compilation results are distinct from clean-machine native installation. No package/release/server mutation in this implementation unit.

requirements.statement: Make novice installation recoverable across application changes and logged-out system confirmation; remove false existing-app detection and verify the current full workbench instead of obsolete legacy screens.
acceptance: An ordinary ChatGPT bundle must not suppress Codex installation. Reuse canonical application identity; an unrelated existing destination must produce an actionable conflict, never installed and never overwrite.

After a global installer job finishes for another selected app, load the selected app plan without repeating mutations or polling ping-pong. Explicit recheck refreshes installer state and discovery; navigation or account/model changes cannot resurrect auto-activation consent.

Windows users can confirm installation without logging in or selecting a model. Checking alone creates no connection intent and never writes credentials; signed-in automatic continuation retains the exact one-use native session and full-selection proof.

Replace seven obsolete legacy App screen assertions with current workbench integration journeys at the native boundary, preserving independent provider/hook/component regressions. Execute all repository Vitest tests and inherited native/cross-platform/build acceptance on the final source state, not merely src tests.

Exercise retry, unavailable progress, unfinished Windows installation, existing destination preservation, logged-out completion and changed selection. Use clear user actions instead of terminal instructions or false completion.

No packaging, release, public binary distribution, server modifications, admin policy changes or overwrite of an installed app. Existing download-origin checks and cross-compilation cannot establish mainland download usability or Windows/Apple-Silicon clean-machine acceptance; report the remaining evidence separately.

contracts.authorization: Bundled desktop webview only. User explicitly starts or cancels an installation, or opens one compiled official guide. Inspect is read-only. No account credentials or caller-controlled URL/path/command. Native request IDs and native job IDs bind retries.

Re-detect before OS write, retain validator-bound package cache for replay, inspect state after lost response. No automatic connection replay across account/selection changes.
contracts.compatibility: Additive v2 native command and optional activation v8 handoff. macOS current-user exclusive installation; Windows system-assisted installation with explicit system confirmation. Existing connect/open/restore behavior remains unchanged.

If Windows offers Reinstall/Replace, tell user to cancel.

macOS mutation retains shutdown admission through copy, exclusive publication and owned mount cleanup. Download cancellation is safe; no cancellation wrapper drops OS mutation. Windows transfers ownership to system UI and releases its own permit after handoff; closing/cancelling Yecai does not cancel that system installer. Keep opened package bytes available.

Only created macOS or explicitly confirmed Windows targets can carry a one-use full-selection/native-epoch activation proof. Fresh discovery must resolve the exact job-associated target; existing, missing or ambiguous targets require manual confirmation.

Network/metadata/cancel failure retains only owned cache. Changed strong validators restart download; absent strong validators prohibit resume, not a fresh complete download. Exact content size/type/redirect checks and native package trust remain mandatory.

Installation success is not connection success. Changed account, model/group/default, line, tool or navigation monotonically invalidates renderer continuation; native activation independently enforces original account epoch and one-use intent. At most one native job and no duplicate start.
Native worker owns cleanup and bounded original-package cache, never arbitrary paths. No public mirror or no-proxy guarantee follows from private server staging.

Deterministic tests must exercise quit before worker start, during download and during OS mutation, plus worker failure/permit release, destination races, Windows handoff ownership and stale/replayed native consent.
Reopen is an explicit user action for a pending Windows system installer only. Recheck cached hash/identity and existing packages; never reopen automatically after polling, restart or lost response.

default.behavior: Show the ordered beginner journey or client security and release truth with clear links to the available local destinations.
default.visibleTruth: The client candidate is usable for local discovery, preview, settings, and explicit diagnostics while backend-dependent and release-signing capabilities remain unavailable.
prohibitedClaims: Do not call the client production-ready, logged in, configured, signed, notarized, auto-updating, or connected to account data.
default.freshness: Candidate capabilities and blockers are compiled into the current application version and have no remote freshness claim.
default.recovery: The user can move to another local destination or restart the application without restoring data.
default.correlation: Static guidance creates no remote or persistent operation identity.

loading.behavior: Reserve a skeleton only for a future signed remote readiness projection and keep all unavailable capabilities disabled.
loading.visibleTruth: RU-005 does not load account, model, price, update, or compatibility data on these pages.
prohibitedClaims: Do not show cached or sample remote facts while a future request is unresolved.
loading.freshness: A future newest request identity would own this state.
loading.recovery: A future failure returns to a truthful unavailable state.
loading.correlation: No request identity exists in RU-005 static pages.

empty.behavior: Explain that no account, model, price, signed-update, or release-signing evidence is available rather than filling the page with default values.
empty.visibleTruth: Remote and release-security facts are absent, while the local candidate features remain separately accessible.
prohibitedClaims: Do not render absence as zero balance, free pricing, no updates, or successful signing.
empty.recovery: A later frozen integration may replace the unavailable sections.

partial.behavior: Show each ready local feature and each blocked remote or release feature independently.
partial.visibleTruth: Only named client-side capabilities are implemented; every backend and signing gate remains explicit.
prohibitedClaims: Do not promote one completed local feature into full V1 or production readiness.
partial.freshness: Each state is tied to the current candidate version.
partial.recovery: Use the corresponding destination; blocked capabilities require a later release.
partial.correlation: Static state has no request identity.

error.behavior: Show a safe client rendering error with no backend, credential, configuration, or update inference.
error.visibleTruth: The page did not render its local projection.
prohibitedClaims: Do not attribute an unclassified client error to the network, account, API, or configuration.
error.recovery: Restart the client; no data rollback is required because static pages write no product data.
error.correlation: Only a safe local error class may be shown.

expired.behavior: Mark any future remote readiness or update evidence stale and retain only compiled candidate facts.
expired.visibleTruth: No stale remote result is current.
prohibitedClaims: Do not keep an expired update, price, model, or account state looking live.
expired.freshness: Compiled facts remain bound to the app version; future remote facts require their own expiry.
expired.recovery: Return to current local candidate truth.
expired.correlation: Expired remote identities are not present in RU-005.

conflict.behavior: Prefer the stricter blocked state if implementation, backend, signing, or update evidence disagrees.
conflict.visibleTruth: The candidate cannot prove the disputed capability.
prohibitedClaims: Do not choose a favorable readiness or release claim from conflicting evidence.
conflict.freshness: Conflict persists until a later accepted decision and verified release unit.
conflict.recovery: Keep the capability disabled and update the governed evidence before release.
conflict.correlation: No secret or raw signing material is displayed.

recovery.behavior: Route the user to the exact local feature or explain which later backend or signing gate is required.
recovery.visibleTruth: Recovery has not completed until the named capability has verified evidence.
prohibitedClaims: Do not offer force-enable, unsigned auto-update, plaintext-key, retained-backup, or fake-login shortcuts.
recovery.freshness: Guidance is fixed to the current candidate version.
recovery.recovery: Use only an available local destination or wait for a later verified release.

processing.behavior: Show processing only when the user has started a local scan or bounded connectivity check on its owning page.

expired.visibleTruth: The superseded result is not current.
prohibitedClaims: Do not merge results or latencies from different requests.
expired.freshness: Only the newest started requestId can own the page.
expired.recovery: Continue waiting for or showing the newest request.

conflict.behavior: Reject any response with duplicated, missing, swapped, or unapproved line identity.
conflict.visibleTruth: The projection cannot prove it belongs to the fixed two-host catalog.
prohibitedClaims: Do not accept a caller-provided or redirected host as an approved line.
conflict.correlation: No host, path, header, or credential supplied by content is executed.

recovery.behavior: Explain whether the bounded evidence was DNS failure, TCP failure, timeout, partial reachability, or invalid projection and offer only retry or navigation.
recovery.visibleTruth: The client has not repaired or modified the network, DNS, proxy, firewall, server, or API.
prohibitedClaims: Do not offer automatic network repair, configuration apply, credential entry, or production changes.
recovery.freshness: Recovery always creates a new request identity.
recovery.recovery: Retry the same two compiled host checks after the user independently changes conditions.

processing.behavior: Run both fixed-host checks concurrently within bounded resolver and connection timeouts.
processing.visibleTruth: No HTTP request, API payload, credential, cookie, model prompt, configuration content, telemetry, or update check is processed.
prohibitedClaims: Do not display successful API or model health while only a socket connection is processing.
processing.freshness: Processing ends at the bounded timeout or a complete two-line projection.
processing.recovery: Each failure becomes a safe result without hiding the other line.
processing.correlation: One requestId owns both transient tasks.

default.behavior: Show the 野菜API welcome shell, the fixed five-tool list, and one primary button labelled to check installed tools.
default.visibleTruth: No discovery result exists yet; the page says that the check is local and read-only and that no API knowledge is required.
prohibitedClaims: Do not claim that any tool is installed, configured, compatible, connected, or ready before a scan result exists.
default.freshness: No result timestamp is shown before the first scan.
default.recovery: The user may start the local scan or close the app without changing the machine.
default.correlation: A requestId is generated only when the user starts a scan.

loading.behavior: Keep all five tool cards visible with per-tool checking indicators and disable duplicate scan submission while the current request is active.
loading.visibleTruth: The page says that local executables and their version output are being checked and that no configuration or network action is running.
prohibitedClaims: Do not show cached installation or compatibility results as the active scan result.
loading.freshness: The active requestId and start time own the pending result.
loading.recovery: If the request fails, transition to error while retaining no invented tool status.
loading.correlation: Only the active requestId may complete this state.

empty.behavior: Show all five tools as not found and explain that this is not an application error.
empty.visibleTruth: The most recent completed local scan found no executable candidate for any supported tool.
prohibitedClaims: Do not claim the tools are uninstalled when they may exist outside the bounded discovery locations.
empty.freshness: Show the completion time of the newest accepted requestId.
empty.recovery: The user may install a tool independently and rescan; RU-001 never installs it.
empty.correlation: Advanced details show the newest accepted requestId without a complete local path.

partial.behavior: Show each of the five tool results independently so found, not-found, failed, timed-out, and read-only states can coexist.
partial.visibleTruth: Only observations from the newest completed local scan appear, including exact version text for successful probes.
prohibitedClaims: Do not promote one tool's success into a claim about another tool or about configuration health.
partial.freshness: All cards share the newest accepted scan completion time.
partial.recovery: A failed or missing tool can be rescanned without hiding valid results for the other tools.
partial.correlation: Every visible card belongs to the same newest requestId.

error.behavior: Show a plain-language scan failure without replacing it with guessed installation results.
error.visibleTruth: The discovery query did not produce a valid complete five-tool projection.
prohibitedClaims: Do not display the previous scan as if it were the failed request's current result.
error.freshness: The failed requestId is identified and prior results are visibly stale or cleared.
error.recovery: Retry creates a new requestId and performs the same bounded read-only scan.
error.correlation: The safe local error class is correlated to the failed requestId; raw command output is not displayed.

expired.behavior: Mark a superseded result as expired and prevent it from overwriting a newer request.
expired.visibleTruth: A scan completion arrived for an older requestId and was rejected from the current projection.
prohibitedClaims: Do not merge cards from different request identities or completion times.
expired.freshness: Only the newest started requestId is eligible to become current.
expired.recovery: Continue showing the newest active or completed request; no filesystem recovery is required.
expired.correlation: Both expired and current request identities remain in transient UI control flow only.

conflict.behavior: Highlight every tool with multiple canonical executable candidates and explain that no candidate was silently chosen.
conflict.visibleTruth: The bounded scan observed more than one distinct executable for at least one tool.
prohibitedClaims: Do not claim compatibility, choose a preferred executable, or expose a configure action while installation identity is ambiguous.
conflict.freshness: Candidate counts come only from the newest accepted scan.
conflict.recovery: The user resolves the tool installation externally, then rescans; RU-001 changes no PATH or tool file.
conflict.correlation: The conflict and sanitized candidate source classes are bound to one requestId.

recovery.behavior: After a failed, timed-out, or superseded scan, explain that a clean rescan is the only in-app recovery action.
recovery.visibleTruth: No write or rollback is necessary because discovery is read-only and stores no retained scan history.
prohibitedClaims: Do not offer repair, install, update, configuration, credential, or restore operations in RU-001.
recovery.freshness: Recovery always creates a new requestId and never mutates an older result.
recovery.recovery: Run another bounded local scan; if it fails again, preserve the truthful per-tool failure states.
recovery.correlation: The recovery request receives its own requestId.

processing.behavior: Represent each bounded version probe as in progress while keeping configuration and remote-service controls absent.
processing.visibleTruth: Only local executable discovery and a bounded --version command may be processing.
prohibitedClaims: Do not imply that login, billing, API connectivity, model retrieval, updates, or configuration are processing.
processing.freshness: Processing belongs to the newest active requestId and expires when it is superseded.
processing.recovery: Each probe times out into a truthful per-tool result; the overall projection still completes when possible.
processing.correlation: Per-tool processing is aggregated under one requestId without persistent telemetry.

packages.objective: Make novice installation recoverable across application changes and logged-out system confirmation; remove false existing-app detection and verify the current full workbench instead of obsolete legacy screens.
deliverables: Recoverable selected-app and logged-out installation UX
Current App integration journeys and full repository test evidence
Scoped acceptance report with real-device and distribution gaps
nonGoals: No server/public installer mirror publication or license assumption
No automatic dependency installation for CLI/DSH/Hermes/OpenClaw yet; official guided help only
No overwrite of existing applications, trust bypass, new account/API/DB or vendor updater changes
No paid live probes, packaging, version bump, signing, release or GitHub push

migrationPolicy.dataBackfill: No DB/config schema changes. New process-owned installer progress and private original-package retry cache only.
migrationPolicy.rollback: Revert client feature without uninstalling applications. Existing connection restoration stays unchanged; remove only owned temporary files when safe.

compatibilityPolicy.strategy: Exclusive current-user Mac installation and explicit Windows App Installer handoff with exact native target/session proof; no silent deployment or existing app replacement.
compatibilityPolicy.supportedVersions: Official currently documented desktop platforms; macOS Intel Codex has no supported package. Windows/macOS compilation and fixtures do not claim clean-machine acceptance.
compatibilityPolicy.removalGate: No existing app/config/secret overwrite, public distribution or forced upgrade.

requiredAcceptanceScenarios.assertion: Native executable fixtures cover download/validator replay, cancellation, stage ordering, no-overwrite, malicious identity/source paths and cross-platform compilation. Include native one-use full-selection/account proof, exclusive destination race, quit-before-spawn, cancelled download, non-cancelled mutation drain, Windows handoff ownership and worker-error permit cleanup. Include identity-aware Mac presence and unrelated destination conflict preservation.

Renderer scenarios prove missing/installed/guided UX, permission and failure recovery, double-click/lost response, cancellation, stale context and exactly-once activation handoff. Include selected-app refresh after another job finishes and logged-out Windows confirmation without auto-activation.
Renderer production build and typecheck plus unchanged release/version/server boundary.

All repository Vitest suites pass, including current App integration journeys, logged-out Windows confirmation and cross-app terminal-state recovery. No skipped failure or pass-count-only readiness claims.

stopConditions: Requires public redistribution permission, CAPTCHA bypass or server changes
Requires replacing existing user applications, admin trust policy changes, live account credentials or paid probes
Frozen IPC/ownership conflict; re-review before implementation
